title: 1986 AHSME Problem 29
statement: Two of the altitudes of the scalene triangle \(ABC\) have length \(4\) and \(12.\) If the length of the third altitude is also an integer, what is the biggest it can be?

solutions.text:
Let the third altitude be \(h.\) Since each side equals twice the common area divided by its altitude, the side lengths are proportional to \[ \frac14,\qquad\frac1{12},\qquad\frac1h. \] The two nontrivial triangle inequalities give \[ \begin{aligned} \frac1h&\lt\frac14+\frac1{12}=\frac13,\\ \frac1h&\gt\frac14-\frac1{12}=\frac16. \end{aligned} \] Thus \(3\lt h\lt6.\) The largest integral possibility is \(5,\) and its three altitudes are distinct as required for a scalene triangle.

Therefore the correct answer is B.
hints: For a fixed triangle area, each side is inversely proportional to its corresponding altitude
Apply the triangle inequalities to side lengths proportional to \(\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{12},\frac{1}{h}\)
